Crest Tracker, powered by Zynthian.

Keep the musical backend. Replace the interaction and presentation with Crest’s compact tracker workspace. Song opens directly into Phrase; Instruments exposes the sounds and routing already owned by Zynthian.

EXISTING BACKENDFRONTEND ADAPTATIONNEW CAPABILITY / DECISION

This is a reviewable plan and an offline interaction demo. It does not connect to Zynthian, send MIDI, produce audio or save a session. Example notes, instruments and mixer values are temporary fixtures. The current runtime remains unchanged.

A shorter musical path

SONGScenes, rows and clip references
›
PHRASEA pad’s notes, in tracker or piano roll
›
INSTRUMENTSLoaded sound, preset, MIDI and effects

Choose a Song cell to open its Phrase. Switch between tracker and piano roll without changing the musical material. Open Instruments to change the sound receiving those events. Back returns to the exact Song cell. A compact menu holds file actions, settings and less frequent tools.

No tracker Chain layer in this version. The Figma’s Chain is an ordered list of phrases. A Zynthian chain is a MIDI/audio processor path. Those are different objects; Zynthian chains remain intact under Instruments and Routing.

Concept mapping

SongADAPTZynSeq scene / launcher / arrangementRender the sequencer overview as rows and track columns. Preserve native repeat, follow, launch and stop behavior. A visual Song is not automatically a new song-file format.
Song rowADAPTA scene’s native phrase row, containing channel sequencesCall this an arrangement row in the interface. Keep native scene, phrase-row and channel IDs behind each cell; never address a clip by its visible row index alone.
PhraseADAPTA pad / clip’s pattern, opened by the pattern editorThe user’s “pad step view” becomes Crest Phrase. Backend objects also named “phrase” are not automatically the same thing. If a clip contains several patterns, preserve their timing and expose them; do not silently flatten them.
TrackDECISIONCurrent launcher columns follow Zynthian chains and their channelsCrest track identity is separate from MIDI channel. Start with 8 visible tracks, configurable 1–16. Independent track targeting, per-note channels and track mute/solo need an explicit adapter contract; the existing launcher is not already an independent tracker.
InstrumentADAPTLoaded chain / processor, engine, bank and presetA named view of a loaded sound and its destination. A preset describes sound settings; it is not a new synth instance or a MIDI channel. Use Zynthian’s installed engines, bank/preset browser, controls and routing.
MIDI ChannelDECISIONZynSeq output and native MIDI routerShow channels 1–16 to the user; preserve backend IDs. Changing a note target must not swap presets or start an engine during playback. Per-note channels may require splitting events across native channel sequences.
Mixer / sendsEXISTINGZynMixer and existing audio routingUse vertical strips, pan, mute/solo and a selected-strip inspector. Mixer strips represent actual chain outputs. Two tracker tracks sharing one destination share that mixer strip; track mute is a separate sequencer action.
Song FileEXISTINGSnapshots, ZS3 and native pattern filesFull session Save/Load uses snapshots. ZS3 recalls performance state; it is not a complete song save. Pattern import/export remains a scoped operation. UI metadata must not become a competing musical database.

Where the rest of Zynthian lives

Two primary editing contexts: Song and Instruments. Mixer is a direct peer shortcut. The menu makes the remaining workflows reachable without putting every backend screen permanently beside the grid. These destinations are proposed coverage, not a claim that this demo implements them.

Runtime versions differ: the controller checkout’s scene/phrase launcher and the packaged stock Oram UI do not expose identical objects. Bind to the connected backend’s reported capabilities and IDs; disable unsupported operations with a reason. Do not present a fabricated “available” screen.

Musical rules to preserve

Notes, sustain and OFF

Empty tracker cells introduce no event and sustain the track’s held note. OFF explicitly releases that track’s held note on its original MIDI channel. Clearing restores empty/sustain. ZynSeq stores durations: the adapter must translate these rules to note lengths and releases, including loop, stop, mute and target-change boundaries.

This demo shows a monophonic track projection: notes extend until the next note, OFF or the pattern end. The piano roll uses the same fixture. Native polyphonic clips must remain polyphonic; they must never be truncated into one row note.

Shared references and undo

A repeated phrase is a reference, not an accidental copy. Before changing shared material, offer Edit Shared or Make Unique, show all uses, and retain stable identities. Native pattern undo/redo stays authoritative once connected. Group edits must form one reversible operation.

Four editors, one musical result

Tracker and piano roll edit the same notes. Euclidean uses steps, hits and rotation; Randomizer uses note/rhythm constraints, seed and locks. Generated previews should commit ordinary events through native editing and undo. They do not create another playback clock or sound engine. Drum-specific editing remains optional.

Timing and expression

Requested settings: 1–64 steps; 1/4 through 1/64 resolution; straight, triplet and dotted timing; tempo, swing, gate, direction, root and scale. Preserve native timing when changing the visual grid. Tracker FX1–3, per-note targets and full MPE expression are not proven end to end; define support and persistence before enabling them.

Controller focus

Cyan marks the editing cursor; green marks playback. Playback must not steal focus. Closing a popover restores its opener; Back returns to the prior location. Every pointer action needs an equivalent controller action. Physical bindings remain provisional; the demo reuses this repository’s existing browser/SDL input map.

Instrument identity

The first version presents loaded Zynthian sounds, not a second preset library. A sound can serve multiple tracks. Preset changes affect that loaded instance and all its users. Figma’s pinned sound revisions and shared instrument library require separate design work; do not claim native equivalents.

Keep ownership below the interface

Crest HTML / JSViews, focus, selections, popovers, capabilities
C++ web host or browserSame frontend; native SDL or browser Gamepad API
Existing Node transport / bridgeCommands, state, errors, stable native identities
Zynthian + native librariesEngines, MIDI/audio routing, clock, notes, undo, snapshots

The existing Python bridge can remain for this work. No engine algorithm, audio path or host packaging needs replacement to build the interface. The frontend requests operations and renders confirmed backend state; it must not treat an optimistic local change as a successful backend save.

Implementation order and proof

  1. Review this interface and vocabulary. Walk Song, Phrase, Instruments and Mixer. Confirm the direct Song/Phrase flow and identify differences from the Figma before changing the running frontend.
  2. Connect read-only views. Replace fixtures with native IDs, scene/clip/pattern state, loaded processors and actual mixer strips. Prove every displayed value agrees with the backend and reconnect restores selection safely.
  3. Connect existing musical actions. Clip launch/stop, piano-roll note edits, native undo, engine/bank/preset, parameters, routing and mixer. Save a snapshot, restart and recall it. Verify actual MIDI/audio separately from browser interaction tests.
  4. Add tracker semantics. Specify independent tracks, duration/sustain/OFF conversion, per-note channels, shared edits and polyphony. Prove exact MIDI events and no held notes after stop, mute, disconnect or loop boundaries. Preserve notes through tracker/piano-roll round trips.
  5. Add creation tools. Implement Euclidean/Randomizer commits, supported FX and expression only after playback and snapshot round trips pass. Consider tracker Chains only if direct phrase references prove insufficient.

  • Existing sequencer adapter: launcher objects, native pattern reads/edits and undo.
  • Current screen coverage: native destinations and integration limits.
  • Shared controller input and C++ web host.
  • Existing manual and sequencer mockups: prior requirements; previews do not establish native playback.
